title: What is known about 1RB0RF_1LC1RE_0LD0LC_1RD0RB_1RA0RB_0LC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_1LC1RE_0LD0LC_1RD0RB_1RA0RB_0LC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is a word of blocks of 1s on the left and a binary counter on the right; the head rewrites the word by a fixed map and counts. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, but it is now a question about a small explicit map. Lean (kernel) proves every kind of macro step the run takes: the six regular steps, the anomalies and all 26 cases of the collision. They are assembled into one function, the macro map, which sends a word-and-counter configuration to the next one, and Lean proves: if the macro map can be applied for ever starting from the configuration reached at step 27, the machine never halts. The map goes through 108 macro steps without failing (Lean, compiled evaluation; this is more than 1.7·109 machine steps) and through 300 anomalies and collisions in the accelerated simulation (about 21248 machine steps). A proof that it never fails would need to control the low binary digits of the counter at every anomaly; they behave like random bits, and we found no way to do that.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: The six regular Q-steps
claims.text: From W 0 1^(3a) B>0 R the machine reaches the next Q configuration after a step count linear in the parameters, in each of the six cases (last block 2j+5, 3, or a 1 after 2i+1; counter low part a+2, or one unit then t gaps of 2): shift rules generated by bbtools.symtm.prove.

claims.title: Q-step = φ twice, counter plus one
claims.text: The same six steps restated on Q configurations qc W a P T: the word goes to phi (phi W) (phi defined on lists) and the counter's low part and gaps update as a binary counter.

claims.title: The anomaly, exactly
claims.text: When the word has run out the machine rewrites it in one sweep, for every value of the parameters and every tape beyond: from 1^(2c+2) 0 1^(3(a+1)) B>0 R (blank to the left) it reaches 1^2 (0 1)^c 0 1^3 B>0 0^(3a) 1 R, one cell further left, in 3a+8c+17 steps; from the word 1^(2c+2) 0 1 with a+2 units it reaches the word 2 1…1 3 with a gap of 3a+1 in 3a+8c+46 steps; with one unit and a first gap 3(p+1)+2 it reaches the regular Q configuration with word 2 1…1 5 and first gap 3p+2 in 8c+57 steps. The new gap is the misaligned one (not of the form 3p+2).

claims.title: The word-and-gap pattern is not an invariant
claims.text: From the Q configuration 1^2 0 1^3 0 1^3 B>0 (a valid word 2 3, a one-unit counter, no gaps, blank tape) the machine halts at step 190. Its word is so short that it runs out a second time before the misaligned gap made by the first anomaly is cleared; the second anomaly leaves gaps of 1 and 0 in a row, and the collision on them halts. So no proof can use only the shape of the word and of the gaps (even/odd blocks, gaps ≡ 2 mod 3): it has to carry the sizes.

claims.title: The collision, in all its cases
claims.text: A collision is the step taken when the counter's low part is one unit, followed by t gaps of length 2 and then a gap g of length 0 or 1. Lean proves what it does for every t, both values of g, any number U of gaps of length 2 behind it, and a next gap of at least 5 cells or blank tape (26 rules): the word takes its usual double step, its last block grows by 2, and the counter's low part is turned into about 3t/2 new blocks at the end of the word; the counter restarts from one unit (or a few, when U ≥ 2) and the next gap is shortened by 3, 4 or 5 cells. The rules do not depend on the word: they are proved for any tape to the left.
claims.where: coll_e0_0_gap … coll_o1_u2_blank, lean/Collide.lean (generated by py/gen_collide.py); restated as zcoll_* in lean/CollideQ.lean; the table is coll in lean/Full.lean

claims.title: The anomaly with a one-unit counter
claims.text: When the word is a block and a single 1 and the counter's low part is one unit followed by t gaps of length 2 and a gap of at least 3 cells (or blank tape), the new word is 2 1…1 5, the low part becomes t+1 units and the gap loses 3 cells, for every value of the parameters (4 rules). Together with the two anomalies above this covers every anomaly of the simulated run.

claims.title: The macro map, and that the machine follows it
claims.text: astep is a function on configurations (W, a, G) (the word's blocks, the counter's low part, the list of gap lengths, standing for the tape W 0 1^(3a) B>0 0^g1 1 0^g2 1 …). It returns the next such configuration: a regular step, an anomaly or a collision, or nothing when none of the proved rules applies. Lean proves that whenever it returns a configuration, the machine really goes from the first tape to the second, in at least 17 steps.

claims.title: Non-halting reduced to the macro map
claims.text: The run from blank tape reaches the configuration W = 2 1, a = 1, no gaps at step 27. Lean proves: if the macro map can be applied any number of times starting there, the machine never halts; and if it can be applied k times, the machine does not halt in its first 27 + 17k steps. So the halting problem of this machine is now the question whether a short explicit function on lists of numbers ever returns nothing.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: 10<sup>8</sup> macro steps without a failure
claims.text: The macro map is applied 10<sup>8</sup> times from the step-27 configuration by compiled evaluation and never fails; with the theorem above the machine does not halt in its first 1,700,000,027 steps (the true count is larger: 17 is only the shortest macro step).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 135 cells have been visited and 62 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: A direct C run (c/fevents.c of the family folder) reaches 2·1010 steps; it has 5 F events (A reading 1), each followed by a 0.

claims.title: Accelerated simulator agrees with direct runs
claims.text: py/hyb.py reproduces every F-event time of the direct run up to 2·1010 steps, and 7 direct runs of 3·108 steps from random mid-phase Q events end where it predicts (for the first machine of the family, also 64,065 consecutive Q events of one phase and 11 more mid-phase checks).

claims.title: 300 transients without a halt
claims.text: The accelerated simulator runs 300 anomalies and collisions from blank tape, up to about 2<sup>1248</sup> steps and a tape 2510 cells wide, with no halt.

claims.title: Shapes of the irregular phases
claims.text: In 300 transients of the accelerated run: all 192 collisions start with the counter's low part one unit, then only gaps of length 2, then a misaligned gap of length 0 (119) or 1 (73); all 108 anomalies start from the word [x] or [x, 1], never with a misaligned gap pending.

claims.title: The race
claims.text: Over 99 epochs (anomaly to anomaly) the collision cascade ends at most 2<sup>32</sup> steps after the anomaly, while the epoch lasts up to 2<sup>1222</sup> steps; the smallest margin is 4.7 bits (1 epoch below 10 bits).

claims.title: The macro map agrees with the machine on 300 transients
claims.text: py/amodel.py is the macro map in Python. Along the accelerated run every anomaly and collision (89 + 11 + 8 anomalies of the three kinds, 192 collisions) was also run cell by cell; the map gives the same configuration each time, and it never fails.

claims.title: When the race is lost
claims.text: After an anomaly from a one-block word, with the new word B bits long (see the explainer) and the counter's low part a units, the first collision comes after exactly 2a − 2 regular steps if a ≤ B − 1; if a ≥ B the word runs out first (checked for B = 2…8, a = 1…9 with the macro map). In the simulated run a is at most 18 while B grows from 7 to over 1200; the smallest B − a after the first three anomalies is 6, and the counter is never longer than B bits.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/fixed
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.037).

claims.title: Why it probably never halts
claims.text: The low part a at an anomaly is one more than the number of trailing zeros of the counter's value at that moment. In the simulated run these values look like random bits: a = 1 about half the time, 2 a quarter of the time, and so on. If they were random, the chance of a ≥ B at an anomaly would be about 2−B, and since B grows by at least 5 at each anomaly the chances add up to less than 2−16 from the fourth anomaly on. This is a heuristic, not a proof: the bits are determined, not random.

claims.title: Gap alignment
claims.text: In every run the gaps behind the first misaligned gap have length ≡ 2 (mod 3), at least 2, so every collision meets a next gap of at least 5 cells, a run of gaps of 2, or blank tape: the cases the macro map covers.
claims.where: observed over all simulated transients; not proved

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. By the Lean reduction it is enough to show that the macro map never fails on the run. It can fail only if a misaligned gap is still there when the word runs out (the race is lost) and the gaps then line up badly. Winning every race needs, at each anomaly, that the counter's value is not divisible by a power of two about as large as the value itself (a ≤ B − 1). That value is the sum of the previous epochs' contributions, shifted and truncated by the collisions; we found no invariant that controls its low digits, and the situation resembles the Collatz-like problems where such digit questions are out of reach. A size bound alone (cascade length against word length) is not preserved from one epoch to the next: the counter may be as long as the word, and only its last digits decide.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine keeps a word of blocks of 1s on the left and a binary counter on the right, and rewrites the word by a fixed map at every count. Every kind of step it takes is now proved in Lean and packed into one small map on lists of numbers; the machine runs for ever if that map never fails. Whether it ever fails comes down to a race that is lost only if the counter shows a very round number at the wrong moment.

facts.text: Regular steps, anomalies and collisions, for all parameters; the machine follows the macro map.
The macro map does not fail; no halt in the first 1.7·10<sup>9</sup> steps.
300 anomalies and collisions simulated; every one matches the macro map.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.037).
After 109 steps the tape spans 135 cells (7 left of the start, 124 right), with a density of 1s of 0.459.

The tape (run-length coded, 1^5 is five 1s, C>0 the head in state C on a 0) at some of the last moments the head reached a new cell, cut to 400 characters:

These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A word and a counter
html: This machine is one of six G12 holdouts that share every transition except two: A1 (0RF or 1RF) and F0. Here A1 is 0RF and F0 is 0LC. Both are used only at an F event, when state A reads a 1, which is rare (see the last section). Everything else is the same for the six machines, and so is this page up to that point.

Most of the time the tape reads W 0 1^(3a) B>0 R. We call this a Q configuration. W is a word: blocks of 1s separated by single 0s, with a blank tape to its left. The first block is even and every later block is odd. R is a run of gaps 0^(3p+2) 1. The run of 3a ones before the head and the gaps together hold a binary counter: a and the gap sizes p are its digits, read in parts. The head stays between the word and the counter. It goes left and rewrites the end of the word, then goes right and adds one to the counter.

On the word the machine applies a fixed map φ. It removes the last block b, adds 2 to the block before it, and appends (b−1)/2 blocks of a single 1. The total width stays the same. Applying it repeatedly, a word with blocks 2 3 1 5 goes like this:

word (blocks)tape
2 3 1 51^2 0 1^3 0 1 0 1^5
2 3 3 1 11^2 0 1^3 0 1^3 0 1 0 1
2 3 3 31^2 0 1^3 0 1^3 0 1^3
2 3 5 11^2 0 1^3 0 1^5 0 1
2 3 71^2 0 1^3 0 1^7

Repeated φ carries every block into the first one: the word eventually becomes a single block. The number of steps this takes is exactly N(W) = Σi≥2 2(Si−1)/2, where Si is the width of the word from block i to the end. So φ is itself a counter, written in a mixed radix.

sections.heading: One Q-step: φ twice, the counter plus one
html: From one Q configuration to the next, the machine applies φ twice to the word and adds one to the counter. The step count is a linear function of the parameters. The step depends only on the last one or two blocks of the word (a last block of 2j+5, a last block of 3, or a last 1 after an odd block) and on the lowest part of the counter (at least two units, or one unit followed by t gaps of length 2). That gives six cases.

word endscountersteps
1^(2j+5)a+2 ≥ 23a + 8j + 41
1^(2j+5)one unit, t short gaps8j + 3t + 41
1^3a+23a + 33
1^3one unit, t3t + 33
1^(2i+1) 0 1a+23a + 8i + 33
1^(2i+1) 0 1one unit, t8i + 3t + 33

All six are Lean theorems checked by the kernel, for every value of the parameters and every tape beyond. lean/Rules.lean states them as shift rules. lean/Macro.lean restates them on Q configurations qc W a P T, with φ defined as a Lean function on lists, for example qstep_big_wide.

sections.heading: Long cycles, anomalies and collisions
html: Between Q events the counter climbs. When it overflows, the run of ones 1^(3k) gets longer by one unit and the counter starts again from zero. A full cycle with counter length k applies φ about 2k times, and each extra unit roughly doubles the time. That is why the right side of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count.

The regular Q-steps break down in two ways, called transients. An anomaly happens when the word has become a single block: φ has nothing left to carry, and the block restarts as 2 1 1 … one cell further left. A collision happens when the counter overflows into a gap that is too short (0 or 1 cells). The accelerated simulator py/hyb.py (in the folder of 1RB0RF_1LC1RE_0LD0LC_1RD0RB_1RA0RB_0LC---) jumps over regular stretches with the closed forms above and runs every transient cell by cell. It agrees with direct simulation on every F event up to 2·1010 steps, and on direct runs of 3·108 steps from Q events picked at random in the middle of phases.
For this machine it ran 300 transients without a halt, up to about 21248 steps, with the tape 2510 cells wide.

sections.heading: The anomaly: the word starts again
html: Each φ moves width into the first block, so after N(W) steps the word is a single block (or a block and a single 1). The next Q-step cannot apply φ and does something else, the anomaly. It is short and exact. The head erases the counter's low part, slides the block one cell to the right through the hole it leaves, and comes back rewriting the block as 1 1 0 1 0 1 …:

beforeaftersteps
1^(2c+2) 0 1^(3a+3) B>0 R1^2 (0 1)^c 0 1^3 B>0 0^(3a) 1 R3a+8c+17
1^(2c+2) 0 1 0 1^(3a+6) B>0 R1^2 (0 1)^c 0 1^3 0 1^3 B>0 0^(3a+1) 1 R3a+8c+46
1^(2c+2) 0 1 0 1^3 B>0 0^(3p+5) 1 R1^2 (0 1)^c 0 1^5 0 1^3 B>0 0^(3p+2) 1 R8c+57

The new word 2 1 1 … 1 has the same width w, and N(W) = 2(w−2)/2 − 1 for it: it lasts that many φ steps. The counter starts again from one unit. Where the old low part was there is now a gap of 3a or 3a+1 cells. That is not of the form 3p+2: it is the misaligned gap. All of the old counter's gaps are still behind it. These are Lean theorems for every a, c and every tape R (anomaly_one, anomaly_two in lean/Transients.lean).

As the new counter overflows, the misaligned gap shrinks by 3 each time. When it is down to 0 or 1, the next overflow is a collision. The head carries that part of the counter into the end of the word, and the next old gap, a few cells shorter, becomes the misaligned one. This cascade continues until the old gaps are used up and the counter is aligned again.

sections.heading: The collision: the counter's low part joins the word
html: After an anomaly the counter has a gap of the wrong length in it: 3p or 3p+1 cells instead of 3p+2. Each time the counter's low part overflows into this gap, the gap loses 3 cells, so it ends at 0 or 1 instead of 2. At the next overflow the regular step is impossible. The counter then reads: one unit, t gaps of length 2, the short gap g. What happens is the same whatever the word:

partbeforeafter
wordWφ(φ(W)), last block + 2, then about 3t/2 new blocks of a single 1 and a last block of 3, 5 or 7
counterone unit, t gaps of 2, gap gone unit (more if gaps of 2 follow)
next gaph + 5h, h + 1 or h + 2

The next gap had the right length 3p+2; after the collision it is 3, 4 or 5 cells shorter. If it lost 3 it is aligned again and the cascade is over. Otherwise it is the new misaligned gap and the story repeats further right. How much it loses depends on whether t is even or odd, on g and on the number U of gaps of length 2 that follow: 26 cases in all, each a Lean theorem for every value of the parameters (lean/Collide.lean; the table is coll in lean/Full.lean).

With these, every step of the run is covered. astep in lean/Full.lean is the whole macro map as one function on triples (word, low part, gaps); Lean proves that the machine follows it (astep_sound) and that the machine never halts if the map never fails from the configuration at step 27 (not_halts_of_arun). Compiled evaluation applies it 108 times without a failure (lean/Bound.lean).

sections.heading: A race between two binary counters
html: The word is itself a binary number. Give each block after the first the weight 2(s−1)/2, where s is the width of the word from that block to its end; the sum N(W) is a number of B = (w−2)/2 binary digits for a word of width w, and φ lowers it by exactly one. So a regular step subtracts 2 from the word's number and adds 1 to the counter. The anomaly is the word's number reaching 0 or 1; it is then set back to all ones, 2B − 1.

Shape alone does not keep the machine running. Lean checks that the Q configuration 1^2 0 1^3 0 1^3 B>0 halts after 190 steps (qc_short_halts): its word is so short that it runs out again while the misaligned gap made by the first anomaly is still there, and the second anomaly then leaves gaps of 1 and 0 in a row. The real run avoids this only because each cascade of collisions ends long before the word runs out.

How long does the first collision take? If the counter's low part at the anomaly was a units, the misaligned gap has about 3a cells and the new counter must count to 2a to close it. The word lasts 2B−1 steps. So the race is won when a ≤ B − 1 and lost when a ≥ B (checked with the macro map for small sizes). Each collision then lengthens the word by about 3t cells, which multiplies its remaining time by about 21.5t, far more than the 2t steps the collision took to arrive; so the first collision is the one that matters.

a − 1 is the number of trailing zeros of the counter's value when the word runs out. In the run the counter is never longer than B digits, so losing the race means the counter shows an extremely round number, one or two leading digits followed only by zeros, exactly at an anomaly. In 108 simulated anomalies a was at most 18, while B went from 7 to over 1200. The values of a look like coin tosses (1 half the time, 2 a quarter of the time, …); if they were, the total chance of ever losing after the first few anomalies would be below 2−16. But nothing we know proves that the round number never comes up: the counter's digits are produced by the earlier epochs in a way that mixes them much like the Collatz map does.

sections.heading: Where it could stop
html: F is reached only from A reading a 1, and F halts on a 1. So a halt needs A to read 1 1. Regular Q-steps never let A read a 1. Only transients do; such a moment is an F event. In the first 2·1010 steps this machine has 5 F events, and at every one the cell after the 1 is a 0.

All the F events we saw happen in collisions. A collision starts when the counter's low part is one unit followed only by gaps of length 2 and then a misaligned gap of length 0 or 1. The head sweeps that part of the counter into the word, and the next gap becomes the misaligned one, shortened by a few cells. A halt needs a gap of length 0 right after such a gap. The gaps behind the misaligned one come from the counter as it was at the anomaly. In every run they have length ≡ 2 (mod 3) and at least 2, so the halt never comes.

Status: open. Lean proves all the macro steps and that the machine never halts unless the macro map fails. The map can fail only after a lost race. That the race is never lost is supported by the simulation and by the heuristic above, not proved.

summary: All macro steps (regular, anomaly, collision) proved in Lean as one map on word-and-counter configurations; if that map never fails the machine never halts (Lean); it does not fail in 10^8 macro steps (Lean, compiled) nor in 300 transients (simulation); whether it ever fails is open and looks Collatz-like.
